newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA GAS OIL/JET-FIRMER OFFERS DESPITE WEAK DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: ASIA GAS OIL/JET-FIRMER OFFERS DESPITE WEAK DEMAND.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices were steady as sellers held out for higher offers, despite limited demand and weaker crude, traders said on Wednesday.
In the Singapore market, offers were seen higher at around $23.00-23.10, compared to recent deals done at $22.40 and $22.50.
Uncertainty about the award level of Taiwan's September gas oil sell tender also kept traders cautious about the direction of the market.
Taiwan was heard to have awarded three cargoes of 0.3-percent gas oil to a Singapore trader at a discount of 20 to 40 cents per barrel under Singapore quotes on a free-on-board (fob) Taiwan basis.
The narrower discounts were for cargoes loading earlier in September.
But the tender results could not be confirmed, with some traders saying that the cargoes were actually awarded at discounts of 50 cents.
Taiwan had earlier said that the bids it received for the tender were in the range of 20-40 cents discount under Singapore quotes, fob.
The next best bid for the tender was heard by a western trader around 40 cents discount.
A major had put in a bid at a 90 cents discount, while a trader bid a discount of 83 cents, traders said.
Enduser demand for jet remains very thin, but prices were also steady on potential buying from traders.
Traders said there would be incentive to buy jet at present since the relatively firm paper levels would allow them to buy physical cargoes at a low price, and sell jet paper at a higher level.
With the market still in contango, buyers could store these jet barrels until the predicted winter demand emerges, they said.
A western trader was heard looking to put jet supplies into a vessel and just float it instead of discharging.
But the same trader was also heard fixing a ship loading jet end this week to Guam, leading traders to believe that it was taking its supplies to its storage facility there.
